cases.text: Tech Lead Backend Engineer. Lead a small Node.js team and design APIs in TypeScript and PostgreSQL.
cases.rationale: Lead changes seniority; backend remains the browseable discipline.

cases.text: Senior Frontend Engineer. Work with React, TypeScript and accessibility. Mentor teammates occasionally.
cases.rationale: Occasional mentoring alone must not promote a senior IC vacancy to LEAD.

cases.text: Principal Data Architect. Own the data platform architecture, Kafka pipelines and warehouse strategy.
cases.rationale: The discipline is data engineering; explicit Principal supports the level.

cases.text: Security Architect. Define cloud security controls and threat modelling for AWS services.
cases.rationale: Architect preserves the security discipline, but the title alone does not establish principal-level scope.

cases.text: CTO for a SaaS startup. Set engineering strategy, hire leaders and remain accountable for platform architecture.
cases.rationale: Executive technical leadership is not silently mapped to a coding specialty.

cases.text: CTO for a marketing agency. Own vendor selection, office IT and business technology budgets.
cases.rationale: A senior title at a technology-using company is not automatically an in-scope engineering role.

cases.text: Software Engineer. Build internal services in Go; the posting gives no clearer product discipline.
cases.rationale: Generic Software Engineer is permitted only as an explicit escape hatch, not a fallback for a known discipline.

cases.text: Software Engineer, backend focus. Design REST APIs, PostgreSQL data models and asynchronous Go services.
cases.rationale: Specific backend evidence beats the generic title.

cases.text: Machine Learning Engineer. Productionize ranking models, feature pipelines and model monitoring.
cases.rationale: ML engineering is an approved distinct discipline.

cases.text: Data Analyst. Build BI dashboards, SQL reports and product metrics for stakeholders.
cases.rationale: Analytics is not silently folded into Data Engineer.

cases.text: Senior QA Automation Engineer. Create Playwright regression suites and CI quality gates.
cases.rationale: Automation QA is more specific than the QA parent role.

cases.text: Manual QA Engineer. Test web releases, write test cases and report defects; no automation responsibilities.
cases.rationale: Manual and automation QA must remain distinguishable.

cases.text: iOS Engineer. Ship native Swift and SwiftUI features for a consumer application.
cases.rationale: The mobile platform is known and should not collapse to a generic mobile role.

cases.text: Cross-platform Mobile Engineer. Build Android and iOS applications in Flutter.
cases.rationale: Cross-platform is distinct from an iOS-only or Android-only role.

cases.text: Product Manager. Define roadmaps, interview customers and coordinate design and engineering teams.
cases.rationale: Product management is out of the approved engineering-role scope.

cases.text: Platform Engineer. Operate Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD for internal developer infrastructure.
cases.rationale: The approved taxonomy treats platform engineering as the DevOps discipline.

cases.text: Software Architect. Own backend architecture for a high-load Java and Spring distributed platform; define service standards, event-driven design, reliability and scaling decisions.
cases.rationale: Draft: broad backend architecture ownership supports Principal while preserving the engineering discipline.

cases.text: Senior Full Stack Engineer in an architecture team. Build reusable Node.js and React foundations, CI/CD tooling and shared development standards for several product teams.
cases.rationale: Draft: architecture-team context does not erase the explicit Senior Full Stack title.

cases.text: Software Architect (.NET). Lead cloud architecture and development of scalable enterprise services, set platform standards, mentor engineers and own complex delivery.
cases.rationale: Draft: .NET service architecture is a backend discipline with cross-platform technical ownership.

cases.text: Software Architect (C#/.NET). Define architecture for transactional backend services, integrations, security, observability and technical standards across engineering teams.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit senior technical scope across backend systems supports Principal.

cases.text: Lead Data Engineer / Solution Architect. Personally build and own architecture for a cloud data platform, data contracts, pipelines, CI/CD and a small delivery pod's technical direction.
cases.rationale: Draft: Lead preserves the Data Engineer discipline; hands-on architecture does not replace it with an Architect role.

cases.text: Software Architect. Set backend direction for a high-load Java and Spring service platform, including distributed systems, messaging, reliability and scalability decisions.
cases.rationale: Draft: second production-derived architecture case for consistency under similar backend evidence.

cases.text: AI Engineer. Build Python AI and machine-learning applications using LLMs, RAG, NLP and SQL; the posting asks for one to two years of relevant experience.
cases.rationale: Draft: no explicit level in the title; this exposes the unresolved years-of-experience policy.

cases.text: Senior BI/Data Engineer. Design ETL/ELT pipelines, data models and analytical systems with Python, SQL, warehouses and BI dashboards.
cases.rationale: Draft: the explicit Senior title and production data-pipeline scope fit Data Engineer.

cases.text: Business Data Analyst. Build product and business analytics, SQL dashboards, cohort analysis and recommendations for product, marketing and finance teams.
cases.rationale: Draft: BI and business analysis remain Data Analyst rather than Data Engineer.

cases.text: Principal AI Engineer. Define AI architecture and strategy; build production ML platforms, LLM systems, RAG, APIs, observability and technical standards across engagements.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit Principal title and organization-wide AI technical ownership.

cases.text: AI Engineer. Build AI agents, Python integrations and LLM-based automation tools; prototype and operate internal systems.
cases.rationale: Draft: clear AI engineering discipline but no explicit level.

cases.text: Senior Data Engineer. Build cloud-native data platforms, streaming pipelines and data contracts with Python, SQL, Spark, warehouses, Kafka and orchestration tools.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit Senior title and unambiguous data-engineering responsibilities.

cases.text: Head of Engineering. Set engineering strategy, build an engineering organization and remain accountable for platform architecture and delivery.
cases.rationale: Draft: technical executive leadership is not silently mapped to a coding specialty.

cases.text: Head of Engineering for a SaaS product. Hire and lead engineering managers, define technical strategy and own delivery quality.
cases.rationale: Draft: executive title and organizational technical accountability; role remains null.

cases.text: Head of Engineering. Lead product engineering, technical planning, hiring and cross-team delivery for a consumer digital product.
cases.rationale: Draft: management scope is technical but has no single browseable discipline.

cases.text: Deputy Head of Engineering. Support engineering strategy, coordinate technical delivery and lead multiple engineering workstreams.
cases.rationale: Draft: deliberate edge case for whether a deputy Head title should remain C_LEVEL.

cases.text: VP of Engineering. Own engineering strategy, leaders, technical delivery and platform reliability across product teams.
cases.rationale: Draft: VP is executive technical leadership, not a coding discipline.

cases.text: Head of Engineering. Set technical direction for game and platform teams, hire leaders and own engineering execution.
cases.rationale: Draft: another technical-executive context with no single IC discipline.

cases.text: Full-Stack Software Engineer. Build and operate web application features across React frontend and backend services.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit full-stack evidence beats the broad Software Engineer wording.

cases.text: Software Engineer (Frontend). Build browser user interfaces, reusable web components and TypeScript application features.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit frontend discipline beats the generic title; level needs reviewer confirmation.

cases.text: Software Engineer. Work across application features and services; the posting does not establish a more specific technical discipline.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit escape hatch for a genuinely generic engineering vacancy.

cases.text: Senior Software Engineer — TypeScript. Build production TypeScript services and application features; no clearer discipline is stated.
cases.rationale: Draft: Senior is explicit, but TypeScript alone should not silently invent a frontend or full-stack discipline.

cases.text: Staff Software Engineer. Work on broad platform engineering problems, system design and cross-team technical initiatives.
cases.rationale: Draft: deliberate edge case; the contract has not yet decided whether Staff maps to Principal.

cases.text: Senior Software Engineer — Frontend. Build browser upload and streaming experiences with modern web technologies.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit Frontend and Senior signals map independently to discipline and level.

cases.text: Team Lead DevOps for a platform team. Lead infrastructure engineers and own Kubernetes, CI/CD, cloud reliability and developer platform practices.
cases.rationale: Draft: team leadership sets LEAD while DevOps remains the discipline.

cases.text: Lead Backend Engineer. Lead backend implementation and technical decisions for APIs, services and data integrations.
cases.rationale: Draft: Lead changes level, not the Backend Engineer role.

cases.text: Team Lead IT Operations. Coordinate internal workplace support, employee devices, access requests and office IT operations.
cases.rationale: Draft: IT support operations are outside the engineering-role scope even with a leadership title.

cases.text: Tech Lead Embedded Linux. Lead the technical direction for Linux software on connected video devices and guide embedded engineers.
cases.rationale: Draft: Embedded remains the underlying discipline; explicit technical lead scope supports LEAD.

cases.text: Team Lead, AI Product Engineering. Lead engineers building AI-powered product features with Go, LLM tools and platform integrations.
cases.rationale: Draft: AI product scope determines discipline; Team Lead determines level.

cases.text: AI Platform Engineer. Operate MLOps and DevOps infrastructure for AI workloads; the posting seeks a strong Senior or Lead engineer.
cases.rationale: Draft: MLOps platform work maps to DevOps; Senior-versus-Lead wording needs reviewer confirmation.

cases.text: Middle React Native Developer. Build Android and iOS mobile application features with React Native.
cases.rationale: Draft: React Native is cross-platform mobile rather than a generic mobile parent role.

cases.text: Senior React Native Developer. Deliver Android and iOS features in a cross-platform mobile application.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit Senior title and React Native cross-platform discipline.

cases.text: Frontend Developer specializing in React Native. Build native-feeling Android and iOS application experiences from a shared codebase.
cases.rationale: Draft: React Native evidence beats the frontend wording for the browseable discipline.

cases.text: Android Engineer. Build and maintain native Android application features with Kotlin and Android platform tooling.
cases.rationale: Draft: native Android is distinct from cross-platform or iOS disciplines.

cases.text: Senior Android Engineer. Own native Android features, mobile architecture and code quality for a consumer application.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit Senior title and Android-specific discipline.

cases.text: React Native Developer. Build cross-platform mobile features, integrations and release-ready Android and iOS applications.
cases.rationale: Draft: React Native maps to Cross-platform Mobile Engineer with no explicit level.

cases.text: Middle General QA Engineer. Test web releases manually and build C# and Playwright automated checks.
cases.rationale: Draft: Playwright automation makes the automation-QA child role more specific than the QA parent.

cases.text: QA Engineer. Test product releases, document test cases and report defects; no automation responsibilities are stated.
cases.rationale: Draft: generic QA remains the parent role without evidence for the manual or automation child.

cases.text: QA Engineer. Validate web application features, investigate defects and collaborate with developers on release quality.
cases.rationale: Draft: no explicit level or automation signal.

cases.text: Senior Manual QA Tester. Plan and execute manual testing, write test cases and validate product releases.
cases.rationale: Draft: explicit Manual and Senior signals.

cases.text: Senior SDET for a data platform. Build automated quality checks, test infrastructure and reliability coverage for query-engine services.
cases.rationale: Draft: SDET and test infrastructure map to Automation QA rather than generic QA.

cases.text: Manual QA. Validate application behavior manually, maintain test cases and communicate defects to the delivery team.
cases.rationale: Draft: Manual QA is a distinct approved discipline with no explicit level.
